title: ईभीको सीट क्षमता र रुट परमिटमाथि छानबिन हुनुपर्छ : सरोज सिटौला
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । विद्युतीय माइक्रोबसको सीट क्षमता परिवर्तन, रुट परमिट वितरण र रात्रिकालीन सेवा सञ्चालनसम्बन्धी निर्णयमाथि निष्पक्ष छानबिन गर्नुपर्ने नेपाल यातायात व्यवसायी राष्ट्रिय महासंघका अध्यक्ष सरोज सिटौलाले बताएका छन् । बिहीबार मकवानपुरको भीमफेदीमा भएको विद्युतीय माइक्रो दुर्घटनाका बारेमा समाजिक सञ्जाल फेसबुकमा लेख्दै यस्तो बताएका हुन् । उक्त दुर्घटनामा १४ जनाको मृत्यु भइसकेको छ । सिटौलाले सुरुमा ९ सिट क्षमताका रूपमा स्वीकृति पाएका विद्युतीय माइक्रोबसलाई कुन आधारमा ११ सिट क्षमतामा परिवर्तन गरियो ? भन्दै सम्बन्धीत सरकारी निकायलाई प्रश्न गरेका छन् । उनले सार्वजनिक गरेको ध्यानाकर्षणपत्रमा विद्युतीय माइक्रोबसको सिट संख्या निर्धारण, प्राविधिक मापदण्ड र रुट परमिट वितरण प्रक्रियामा गम्भीर प्रश्न रहेको उल्लेख गरेका छन् । उनले ९ सिट क्षमताका सवारीसाधनलाई ११ सिटमा परिवर्तन गर्दा अपनाइएको प्राविधिक आधार, कानुनी प्रक्रिया र मापदण्ड सार्वजनिक गर्न माग गरेका छन् । यात्रुको सुरक्षालाई ध्यानमा राखेर सिट संख्या परिवर्तन गरिएको हो वा अन्य कुनै स्वार्थ र दबाबमा निर्णय भएको हो भन्ने विषय स्पष्ट हुनुपर्ने उनको भनाइ छ । यस विषयमा यातायात व्यवस्था विभाग, प्रदेश सरकार र यातायात कार्यालयहरूको पटक–पटक ध्यानाकर्षण गराउँदा पनि सुनुवाइ नभएको उनको आरोप छ । नागरिकको जीवनसँग प्रत्यक्ष जोडिएको विषयमा सम्बन्धित निकायले गम्भीरता नदेखाएको उनको भनाइ छ । त्यस्तै, विद्यमान कानुनी व्यवस्था र मापदण्डले रात्रिकालीन सेवा सञ्चालन, माइक्रोबसको रुट परमिट तथा प्राविधिक क्षमतासम्बन्धी विषयमा तोकेका सीमाभन्दा बाहिर गएर अनुमति दिइएको भए त्यसको जिम्मेवारी सम्बन्धित पदाधिकारीले लिनुपर्ने उनले बताएका छन् । सिटौलाले ९ सिट क्षमताका सवारीसाधनलाई ११ सिटमा परिवर्तन गर्ने निर्णयको प्राविधिक तथा कानुनी आधार सार्वजनिक गर्न, रुट परमिट वितरण र रात्रिकालीन सेवा सञ्चालनसम्बन्धी निर्णयको निष्पक्ष छानबिन गर्न माग गरेका छन् । कानुनविपरीत परमिट वितरण भएको पाइएमा निर्णय गर्ने र कार्यान्वयन गराउने पदाधिकारीलाई कारबाही गर्नुपर्ने उनको माग छ । यसैगरी, विद्युतीय माइक्रोबसको प्राविधिक अवस्था, यात्रु क्षमता, ब्याट्री, ब्रेक प्रणाली र समग्र सुरक्षा मापदण्डको तत्काल परीक्षण तथा पुनरावलोकन गर्नुपर्ने उनले बताए । दुर्घटना भएपछि मात्रै उद्धार, उपचार र क्षतिपूर्तिको विषय उठाउनुभन्दा दुर्घटना हुनुअघि नै सम्भावित जोखिम पहिचान गरी सुधार गर्नुपर्नेमा अध्यक्ष सिटौलाले जोड दिएका छन् । ‘यातायात क्षेत्रको विकास भनेको सवारीसाधनको संख्या बढाउनु मात्र होइन, यात्रुको जीवन सुरक्षित बनाउनु पनि हो । राजस्वभन्दा नागरिकको जीवन ठूलो हो र परमिटभन्दा यात्रुको सुरक्षा ठूलो हो,’ सिटौलाको ध्यानाकर्षणपत्रमा उल्लेख छ । Kathmandu: Saroj Sitaula, president of the National Federation of Nepal Transport Entrepreneurs, has said that there should be an impartial investigation into the decisions regarding changing the seat capacity of electric microbuses, distribution of route permits, and operation of night services. He said this while writing on social media Facebook about the electric micro accident that occurred in Bhimphedi, Makawanpur on Thursday. 14 people have died in the accident. Sitaula has questioned the relevant government body on what basis was the electric microbus, which was initially approved as a 9-seat capacity, changed to an 11-seat capacity? In the public notice, he has mentioned that there are serious questions in the determination of the number of seats, technical standards and route permit distribution process of the electric microbus. He has demanded that the technical basis, legal process and criteria adopted while converting 9-seat vehicles to 11-seat ones be made public. He said that it should be clear whether the number of seats was changed keeping in mind the safety of passengers or whether the decision was made under any other vested interests and pressure. He alleged that despite repeatedly drawing the attention of the Department of Transport Management, the provincial government and the transport offices on this issue, no attention was paid. He said that the concerned bodies have not shown seriousness in matters directly related to the lives of citizens. Similarly, if permission has been given beyond the limits specified by the existing legal system and standards regarding night service operation, microbus route permits and technical capacity, the concerned officials should take responsibility for it, he said. Sitaula has demanded that the technical and legal basis for the decision to convert 9-seat vehicles to 11-seat ones be made public, and that an impartial investigation be conducted into the decisions regarding route permit distribution and night service operation. He has demanded that action be taken against the officials who made the decision and implemented it if it is found that permits were distributed against the law. Similarly, he said that the technical condition, passenger capacity, battery, brake system and overall safety standards of electric microbuses should be immediately tested and reviewed. Chairman Sitaula emphasized that potential risks should be identified and improved before an accident occurs, rather than raising the issue of rescue, treatment and compensation only after an accident. "Development of the transport sector is not only about increasing the number of vehicles, but also about making the lives of passengers safer. Citizens' lives are more important than revenue and passenger safety is more important than permits," Sitaula's letter of appeal states.

कार्यान्वयन गराउने पदाधिकारीलाई कारबाही गर्नुपर्ने उनको माग छ । यसैगरी, विद्युतीय माइक्रोबसको प्राविधिक अवस्था, यात्रु क्षमता, ब्याट्री, ब्रेक प्रणाली र समग्र सुरक्षा मापदण्डको तत्काल परीक्षण तथा पुनरावलोकन गर्नुपर्ने उनले बताए । दुर्घटना भएपछि मात्रै उद्धार, उपचार र क्षतिपूर्तिको विषय उठाउनुभन्दा दुर्घटना हुनुअघि नै सम्भावित जोखिम पहिचान गरी सुधार गर्नुपर्नेमा अध्यक्ष सिटौलाले जोड दिएका छन् । ‘यातायात क्षेत्रको विकास भनेको सवारीसाधनको संख्या बढाउनु मात्र होइन, यात्रुको जीवन सुरक्षित बनाउनु पनि हो । राजस्वभन्दा नागरिकको जीवन ठूलो हो र परमिटभन्दा यात्रुको सुरक्षा ठूलो हो,’ सिटौलाको ध्यानाकर्षणपत्रमा उल्लेख छ । Kathmandu: Saroj Sitaula, president of the National Federation of Nepal Transport Entrepreneurs, has said that there should be an impartial investigation into the decisions regarding changing the seat capacity of electric microbuses, distribution of route permits, and operation of night services. He said this while writing on social media Facebook about the electric micro accident that occurred in Bhimphedi, Makawanpur on Thursday. 14 people have died in the accident. Sitaula has questioned the relevant government body on what basis was the electric microbus, which was initially approved as a 9-seat capacity, changed to an 11-seat capacity? In the public notice, he has mentioned that there are serious questions in the determination of the number of seats, technical standards and route permit distribution process of the electric microbus. He has demanded that the technical basis, legal process and criteria adopted while converting 9-seat vehicles to 11-seat ones be made public. He said that it should be clear whether the number of seats was changed keeping in mind the safety of passengers or whether the decision was made under any other vested interests and pressure. He alleged that despite repeatedly drawing the attention of the Department of Transport Management, the provincial government and the transport offices on this issue, no attention was paid. He said that the concerned bodies have not shown seriousness in matters directly related to the lives of citizens. Similarly, if permission has been given beyond the limits specified by the existing legal system and standards regarding night service operation, microbus route permits and technical capacity, the concerned officials should take responsibility for it, he said. Sitaula has demanded that the technical and legal basis for the decision to convert 9-seat vehicles to 11-seat ones be made public, and that an impartial investigation be conducted into the decisions regarding route permit distribution and night service operation. He has demanded that action be taken against the officials who made the decision and implemented it if it is found that permits were distributed against the law. Similarly, he said that the technical condition, passenger capacity, battery, brake system and overall safety standards of electric microbuses should be immediately tested and reviewed. Chairman Sitaula emphasized that potential risks should be identified and improved before an accident occurs, rather than raising the issue of rescue, treatment and compensation only after an accident. "Development of the transport sector is not only about increasing the number of vehicles, but also about making the lives of passengers safer. Citizens' lives are more important than revenue and passenger safety is more important than permits," Sitaula's letter of appeal states.

काठमाडौं । विद्युतीय माइक्रोबसको सीट क्षमता परिवर्तन, रुट परमिट वितरण र रात्रिकालीन सेवा सञ्चालनसम्बन्धी निर्णयमाथि निष्पक्ष छानबिन गर्नुपर्ने नेपाल यातायात व्यवसायी राष्ट्रिय महासंघका अध्यक्ष सरोज सिटौलाले बताएका छन् । बिहीबार मकवानपुरको भीमफेदीमा भएको विद्युतीय माइक्रो दुर्घटनाका बारेमा समाजिक सञ्जाल फेसबुकमा लेख्दै यस्तो बताएका हुन् । उक्त दुर्घटनामा १४ जनाको मृत्यु भइसकेको छ । सिटौलाले सुरुमा ९ सिट क्षमताका रूपमा स्वीकृति पाएका विद्युतीय माइक्रोबसलाई कुन आधारमा ११ सिट क्षमतामा परिवर्तन गरियो ? भन्दै सम्बन्धीत सरकारी निकायलाई प्रश्न गरेका छन् । उनले सार्वजनिक गरेको ध्यानाकर्षणपत्रमा विद्युतीय माइक्रोबसको सिट संख्या निर्धारण, प्राविधिक मापदण्ड र रुट परमिट वितरण प्रक्रियामा गम्भीर प्रश्न रहेको उल्लेख गरेका छन् । उनले ९ सिट क्षमताका सवारीसाधनलाई ११ सिटमा परिवर्तन गर्दा अपनाइएको प्राविधिक आधार, कानुनी प्रक्रिया र मापदण्ड सार्वजनिक गर्न माग गरेका छन् । यात्रुको सुरक्षालाई ध्यानमा राखेर सिट संख्या परिवर्तन गरिएको हो वा अन्य कुनै स्वार्थ र दबाबमा निर्णय भएको हो भन्ने विषय स्पष्ट हुनुपर्ने उनको भनाइ छ । यस विषयमा यातायात व्यवस्था विभाग, प्रदेश सरकार र यातायात कार्यालयहरूको पटक–पटक ध्यानाकर्षण गराउँदा पनि सुनुवाइ नभएको उनको आरोप छ । नागरिकको जीवनसँग प्रत्यक्ष जोडिएको विषयमा सम्बन्धित निकायले गम्भीरता नदेखाएको उनको भनाइ छ । त्यस्तै, विद्यमान कानुनी व्यवस्था र मापदण्डले रात्रिकालीन सेवा सञ्चालन, माइक्रोबसको रुट परमिट तथा प्राविधिक क्षमतासम्बन्धी विषयमा तोकेका सीमाभन्दा बाहिर गएर अनुमति दिइएको भए त्यसको जिम्मेवारी सम्बन्धित पदाधिकारीले लिनुपर्ने उनले बताएका छन् । सिटौलाले ९ सिट क्षमताका सवारीसाधनलाई ११ सिटमा परिवर्तन गर्ने निर्णयको प्राविधिक तथा कानुनी आधार सार्वजनिक गर्न, रुट परमिट वितरण र रात्रिकालीन सेवा सञ्चालनसम्बन्धी निर्णयको निष्पक्ष छानबिन गर्न माग गरेका छन् । कानुनविपरीत परमिट वितरण भएको पाइएमा निर्णय गर्ने र कार्यान्वयन गराउने पदाधिकारीलाई कारबाही गर्नुपर्ने उनको माग छ । यसैगरी, विद्युतीय माइक्रोबसको प्राविधिक अवस्था, यात्रु क्षमता, ब्याट्री, ब्रेक प्रणाली र समग्र सुरक्षा मापदण्डको तत्काल परीक्षण तथा पुनरावलोकन गर्नुपर्ने उनले बताए । दुर्घटना भएपछि मात्रै उद्धार, उपचार र क्षतिपूर्तिको विषय उठाउनुभन्दा दुर्घटना हुनुअघि नै सम्भावित जोखिम पहिचान गरी सुधार गर्नुपर्नेमा अध्यक्ष सिटौलाले जोड दिएका छन् । ‘यातायात क्षेत्रको विकास भनेको सवारीसाधनको संख्या बढाउनु मात्र होइन, यात्रुको जीवन सुरक्षित बनाउनु पनि हो । राजस्वभन्दा नागरिकको जीवन ठूलो हो र परमिटभन्दा यात्रुको सुरक्षा ठूलो हो,’ सिटौलाको ध्यानाकर्षणपत्रमा उल्लेख छ ।

Kathmandu: Saroj Sitaula, president of the National Federation of Nepal Transport Entrepreneurs, has said that there should be an impartial investigation into the decisions regarding changing the seat capacity of electric microbuses, distribution of route permits, and operation of night services. He said this while writing on social media Facebook about the electric micro accident that occurred in Bhimphedi, Makawanpur on Thursday. 14 people have died in the accident. Sitaula has questioned the relevant government body on what basis was the electric microbus, which was initially approved as a 9-seat capacity, changed to an 11-seat capacity? In the public notice, he has mentioned that there are serious questions in the determination of the number of seats, technical standards and route permit distribution process of the electric microbus. He has demanded that the technical basis, legal process and criteria adopted while converting 9-seat vehicles to 11-seat ones be made public. He said that it should be clear whether the number of seats was changed keeping in mind the safety of passengers or whether the decision was made under any other vested interests and pressure. He alleged that despite repeatedly drawing the attention of the Department of Transport Management, the provincial government and the transport offices on this issue, no attention was paid. He said that the concerned bodies have not shown seriousness in matters directly related to the lives of citizens. Similarly, if permission has been given beyond the limits specified by the existing legal system and standards regarding night service operation, microbus route permits and technical capacity, the concerned officials should take responsibility for it, he said. Sitaula has demanded that the technical and legal basis for the decision to convert 9-seat vehicles to 11-seat ones be made public, and that an impartial investigation be conducted into the decisions regarding route permit distribution and night service operation. He has demanded that action be taken against the officials who made the decision and implemented it if it is found that permits were distributed against the law. Similarly, he said that the technical condition, passenger capacity, battery, brake system and overall safety standards of electric microbuses should be immediately tested and reviewed. Chairman Sitaula emphasized that potential risks should be identified and improved before an accident occurs, rather than raising the issue of rescue, treatment and compensation only after an accident. "Development of the transport sector is not only about increasing the number of vehicles, but also about making the lives of passengers safer. Citizens' lives are more important than revenue and passenger safety is more important than permits," Sitaula's letter of appeal states.
